_comment: Step 8. The roster is a RULE, not a list: tier N stats are base * growth^N, generated at load up to maxTier.
_ladderComment: Version 6 BOUNDS the ladder at three tiers with big steps, where it used to run twenty tiers with gentle ones. The two are alternatives and cannot be mixed. The old rule ended matches by arithmetic: growth was geometric and the tiers never stopped, so creep HP passed any maze eventually and somebody always lost. x5 cannot go back to twenty tiers either -- 5^19 overflows the 32-bit gold hash and 1.45^19 does not, which is why the step size and the tier count had to move together. THERE IS CURRENTLY NO REPLACEMENT FOR THAT GUARANTEE, and it is a known, deliberate gap rather than an oversight. Measured with `pnpm --filter @ltw/harness lap`: a maze saturates at 50 level-3 towers needing 40,572 HP to survive one lap (80 and 120 towers add nothing, because the route is fixed and the extra towers cannot reach it), while the heaviest creep this ladder can ever produce is Tank III at 250*5^2 = 6,250. Creeps are short by 6.5x, permanently. Two players who both build past 50 towers can therefore sit in a match that cannot end. Bots do not reach it -- MAX_TOWER_TARGET is 45, just under saturation, and mirror matches still decide in 4 to 17 minutes -- so the decision was to ship this and find out whether real play ever gets there before building a valve for it. See the P1 in TODOS.md for the shape a valve would take.
_pacingComment: Unlocks at 0:00, 5:00 and 10:00 rather than every 30 seconds. The x5 step is what makes those two moments matter: a maze built for tier 1 is visibly inadequate the instant tier 2 lands, so both are forced reinvestment beats rather than a number quietly ticking up every half minute. Speed is held constant per archetype; the source table drifts it up a little per tier (swarm 1.5 to 1.7 tiles/s, runner 3.0 to 3.5) and that is deliberately not reproduced, because speed is not part of the growth rule and a per-tier speed column would be a schema change to buy a difference nobody can feel.
_atomComment: ONE PURCHASE IS ONE CREEP. Swarm used to ship a pack of six, so a single click put six creeps in the lane and there was no way to send fewer -- the multiplication happened here, in the data, where no amount of work on the button could reach it. `count` is 1 for every archetype and a pack is something the player assembles by clicking, which is how the map this game descends from has always worked: a shrine click queues one unit and spamming is the intended way to mass-send. Splash still has swarms to answer, because five clicks still produce five creeps; they now cost five decisions instead of one.
_scaleComment: Every gold figure is x10 the source table, so a pack price can be divided by its pack size without rounding away a tenth of the card, and so a bounty of half a gold can exist at all. Gold is hashed as a 32-bit integer (`hash.ts`), so sub-unit prices are not available at any scale -- the scale is the room to express them. Swarm's cost and income are the table's pack figures divided by five, 10/5 and 1/5, then x10.
_sendUnlockComment: The opening build phase, in ticks at 20Hz. Sending was legal from tick 0, which meant the first wave could be in your lane before you had placed a single tower -- there was no opening, just a scramble. 400 is 20 seconds: enough to spend the opening purse as a maze rather than a reflex, and far short of the 6000-tick tier-1 unlock so that unlock stays its own separate beat.

growth._comment: Per tier, and the shape changed with the ladder. hp used to sit ABOVE cost so HP per gold ROSE as you bought up, which was the mechanism that let a creep eventually beat any maze. That mechanism is gone: with three tiers there is no 'eventually' to reach, and nothing carries the guarantee in its place yet -- see _ladderComment. hp and cost now move together at x5, so HP per gold is FLAT and buying up concentrates threat rather than buying it more cheaply. income also x5, so income per gold stays constant within an archetype and the cheap-card-earns-more rule keeps holding at every tier. bounty grows slower than cost at x4, which is the tax falling from about 25% of a tier-1 card to about 15% of a tier-3 one: early sends are economy, late sends are pressure.
